newsitem.title: INDIA: Restricted inflows boost Indian sugar prices.
newsitem.headline: Restricted inflows boost Indian sugar prices.

text.p: Indian sugar prices rose on Tuesday helped by restricted inflows because of higher outstation demand, dealers said.
"Mill inflows were restricted due to higher outstation demand reported at the mill level," one dealer said.
Trading volumes were however low due to the absence of top traders who were attending the funeral of the mother of the president of the Bombay Sugar Merchants Association who died on Tuesday morning.
Ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 7/10 rupees to 1,250/1,275 rupees while M-30 gained by five rupees to 1,275/1,325.
